title: Bitcoin's 2017 bull run and 2018 crash
summary: BTC 2017-18 cycle (Bitstamp daily): peak close $19,188 (2017-12-16), trough $3,180 (2018-12-15), -83%. RSI peaked at 94. Death cross 2018-03-31. $6k support held Feb-Oct 2018 and broke in Nov 2018. Educational only, not financial advice.

title: Strategy overview (paper trading only)
summary: Global rules (top-20 universe, max 1% risk per trade, stop and target logged before entry, 2:1 minimum reward:risk, -3% daily loss limit, no leverage or shorting) plus four strategies: trend following, Donchian breakout, RSI/Bollinger mean reversion, and DCA as the benchmark. Educational only, not financial advice.

title: S1 trend rule tested on Bitcoin's 2017 boom and 2018 crash
summary: Playbook S1 on Bitstamp BTC daily, 2017 to Mar 2019, $2,000 paper account with 1% risk: ended $2,379 (+19%), worst drawdown -4.5%, 16 trades (62% winners). Buy and hold made +286% but fell about 83%. The trend filter sat in cash after the 2018-03-31 death cross. One coin, one cycle, in-sample, so not proof. Educational only, not financial advice.

title: Bitcoin 2020–2021: COVID crash, halving, and the double-top bull market
Bitcoin 2022–2023: the crypto-credit bear market and the recovery
S1 trend rule re-tested on Bitcoin 2020–2022 (rules written before this test)
summary: Year-end S1 equity: $2,309 (2020), $2,302 (2021), $2,302 (2022). The two biggest wins, Oct–Nov 2020 (+8.9R) and Nov 2020–Jan 2021 (+5.4R), made nearly all the profit, the same "few big winners" shape as 2017. The rule took no trades in 2022: the 50-day was under the 200-day from the 2022-01-15 death cross (per Sequoia's note) all year, so it sat out the slide.
